question: There are concerns that the European Banking Authority’s Q&A 2022_6336 adopts a narrow interpretation of the contractual relationship between issuers and merchants, and of the transfer of e-money to merchants, which may not take sufficient account of the way in which four-party payment schemes and other e-money arrangements function and, if applied to such schemes/arrangements, could prevent such products from continuing to operate. In view of the above: 1.

How does the Commission consider the interpretation set out in the European Banking Authority’s Q&A 2022_6336, in particular the requirement for the transfer of e-money to the merchant, to be compatible with the E-Money Directive1 and the relevant caselaw?

Is the Commission considering clarifying that e-money products operating through fourparty payment schemes and other e-money arrangements should not be regarded as falling within the scope of Q&A 2022_6336?

What assessment has the Commission made of the potential impact of this interpretation on existing prepaid card programmes, financial inclusion initiatives and other established e-money products if they were to be reclassified outside of the e-money framework?

Directive 2009/110/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 September 2009 on the taking up, pursuit and prudential supervision of the business of electronic money institutions amending Directives 2005/60/EC and 2006/48/EC and repealing Directive 2000/46/EC (OJ L 267, 10.10.2009, p. 7, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2009/110/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.11.2026) Article 2, point (2), of Directive 2009/110/EC (‘E-Money Directive’)1 defines the notion of emoney2. That definition is technologically neutral and does not make a distinction between emoney that is held on a payment device, and e-money that is stored remotely at a server and managed by the e-money holder through a specific account for e-money.

To have a harmonised approach and in line with the Court’s ruling in case C-661/223, the Q&A 2022_63364 specifies that the acceptance of e-money entails its transferability and voluntary acceptance as a separate monetary asset, and not simply in scriptural money as part of the redemption process.

Existing business models and products currently operating in the EU market can continue to be offered whilst in certain cases there might be a need for re-qualification of the services provided. In such cases, electronic money institutions will have to first assess the method of own funds calculation they have historically applied and to re-calculate their own funds requirements.

Moreover, it would be necessary to update the passport notifications to reflect the correct qualification of the undertaken activities as well as correct reporting of the services provided. The Commission notes that the E-Money Directive will be integrated into the Payments Services Directive5, which has been politically agreed6 and is expected to be published early 20277.

At this stage, the Commission does not consider it necessary to further clarify the definition of e-money and the scope of the interpretation of Q&A 2022_6336. However, the 1 Directive 2009/110/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 September 2009 on the taking up,

pursuit and prudential supervision of the business of electronic money institutions amending Directives 2005/60/EC and 2006/48/EC and repealing Directive 2000/46/EC (OJ L 267, 10.10.2009, p. 7, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2009/110/oj).

2 Article 2 (2) of the E-Money Directive defines electronic money as ‘electronically, including magnetically, stored monetary value as represented by a claim on the issuer which is issued on receipt of funds for the purpose of making payment transactions as defined in point 5 of Article 4 of Directive 2007/64/EC, and which is accepted by a natural or legal person other than the electronic money issuer’.

3 Judgement of the Court of 22 February 2024, ABC Projektai’ UAB, C-661/22, ECLI:EU:C:2024:148, paragraph 47: ‘Although an entry in a payment account also represents a claim, expressed in monetary value, on the institution concerned vis-à-vis a user of its services which has been issued on receipt of funds, it may be inferred from that definition of electronic money provided in Article 2(2) of Directive 2009/110 that the issuance of electronic money is distinct from the mere entry in a payment account in that, inter alia, before being used for the purposes of such a payment, such money must be electronically ‘stored’, which implies that it has been issued beforehand, that is to say, converted into a monetary asset separate from the funds received, and that its use as a means of payment is accepted by a natural or legal person other than the electronic money issuer.
